title: 2027-08-01-precision-contrast-lab-demo
next_steps: Send sandbox access and qprofile CSV
Share performance heatmap and latency traces
Schedule 2-week pilot kickoff w/ infra team
action_items: Ben Carter: Send sandbox invite + qprofile template by 2027-08-03
Priya Nair: Run initial INT8 vs FP8 cold-start bench and share artifacts by 2027-08-06
Miguel Alvarez: Provide sample request distribution and SLOs by 2027-08-04
summary: Optimize Console walkthrough focused on contrast between INT8 and FP8 precision profiles. Demo included console QProfile selector, live benches showing tail latency and throughput, and discussion of fallback rules and quality regressions. Customer concerned about hallucination risk and latency spikes during cold cache. Agreed next steps to run pilot in sandbox and exchange sample workload traces.
topics: Cache warming and KV cache impacts
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-01 15:00 UTC | Duration 62m | Attendees: Ben Carter, Priya Nair (Redwood); Jamie Ortiz, Sara Kim, Miguel Alvarez, Tina Park (Lumenary Health)

[00:00] Ben Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Jamie Ortiz: Jamie here.
[00:14] Sara Kim: Sara.
[00:15] Miguel Alvarez: Miguel, hi.
[00:18] Tina Park: Tina.
[00:22] Ben Carter: Great, so agenda — short console demo of Optimize qprofiles, then live bench numbers INT8 vs FP8, then discuss rollout/fallbacks, questions. Priya will drive the bench.
[00:38] Priya Nair: Hi all. I'm gonna share my screen, give me a sec, looks like it's loading.
[01:02] Priya Nair: Ok, screen share up. First off quick note: our qprofile UI groups by "latency-first" and "fidelity-first" presets, you can customize token-level thresholds. We built the selector to show expected P50/P95/P99 based on your sample trace.
[01:23] Sara Kim: Quick question — when you say P99, is that with cold KV cache or warmed?
[01:30] Priya Nair: Good catch. The baseline here is warm cache with typical prefix caching enabled. We have separate columns for cold-start — you'll see those in the bench.
[01:42] Ben Carter: we'll also show what happens when you switch autoscale policies and burst capacity.
[01:50] [02:10] Priya Nair: Alright jumping into profiles: first profile is INT8-aggressive, quantization at INT8 with per-layer calibration. Note: some layers are quantized with symmetric 8-bit while others use FP16 fallback. The console flags that for you.
[02:32] Miguel Alvarez: sorry, per-layer? is that automatic or we pick layers?
[02:36] Priya Nair: It's automatic by default. You can pin layers if you want more control. The auto-calibrator uses a small calibration set — usually a few hundred samples.
[03:01] [03:15] Priya Nair: Now FP8 profile — it's lexically less lossy on many generative tasks; we see higher charging for throughput but often better quality on nuanced prompts.
[03:30] Tina Park: "Charging"? do you mean cost.
[03:33] Priya Nair: Sorry, yes cost — throughput per GPU is higher, meaning fewer GPUs needed but sometimes more flops, depends on backend.
[03:50] [04:05] Ben Carter: I'm gonna flip to a real customer-weighted bench. This is Lumenary's sample trace we ingested earlier — 40k requests/day, 1.2k p95/day bursts, average prompt 180 tokens.
[04:28] Sara Kim: that's close to our number, except our morning batch is spiky.
[04:35] Priya Nair: On the console page you'll see predicted latency distributions. Here INT8Agg shows P50 28ms P95 160ms P99 420ms (warm). FP8 profile shows P50 24ms P95 120ms P99 350ms. Cold starts add ~200-400ms at tail depending on KV cache hit.
[05:02] [05:18] Jamie Ortiz: FP8 looks better on tail. Why would we ever choose INT8 then?
[05:23] Priya Nair: Good question. INT8 often has the lowest steady-state cost, especially when throughput is dominated by token compute and you can tolerate a small quality delta. Some tasks (long-context summarization, medical text) are more sensitive — that's where FP8 helps.
[05:44] [06:00] Ben Carter: Also note model variants: our routing can fallback to an FP8-variant for flagged prompts or for requests that fail quality checks. Means you can run primarily INT8 and spill to FP8 for safety.
[06:22] Miguel Alvarez: is fallback synchronous? doesn't that double latency if it triggers?
[06:28] Priya Nair: We implement async-check + speculative execution in some cases. Two flavors: speculative parallel (send both INT8 and FP8, take first acceptable) or sequential (re-run on failure). Parallel increases cost but keeps tail low.
[06:48] [07:05] Sara Kim: Could you show an example where FP8 prevented a hallucination?
[07:12] Priya Nair: I have one. Loading eval sandbox.. here is a clinical Q/A prompt. On INT8 the model invented a medication name ~30% of trials; FP8 reduced that to ~6%. I should caveat the sample size is small but consistent across runs.
[07:41] [08:00] Ben Carter: We also attach a quality monitor that runs a small set of eval prompts continuously, will flag regression by profile.
[08:12] Tina Park: How noisy are those monitors? false positives?
[08:20] Priya Nair: We tune thresholds to your tolerance; you can set a guardrail that triggers routing to FP8 automatically or sends an alert and human review.
[08:35] [09:00] Jamie Ortiz: Ok show me the console rules for that.
[09:05] Priya Nair: In Rules -> Fallbacks. You can choose metric (bleu, rouge, domain-specific classifier) and set threshold. If threshold violated, route to fallback model variant or route to a dedicated pool.
[09:29] Ben Carter: We recommend a canary first — run 10% traffic through fallback for a week and monitor.
[09:38] [10:00] Priya Nair: Switching to the live bench tab. I'm going to run a quick compare — executing 500 synthetic requests from your trace at 1rps to emulate tails. Note: network emulation sim is approximate.
[10:25] [10:40] Priya Nair: Running INT8 first. Results streaming: median 30ms, p95 170ms, p99 410ms, tokens/sec 320. Error rate 0.7% (quality classifier).
[11:02] [11:20] Priya Nair: FP8 run now — median 26ms, p95 125ms, p99 340ms, tokens/sec 360. Error rate 0.2%.
[11:42] Miguel Alvarez: those p99 improvements are material. What about GPU utilization?
[11:48] Priya Nair: INT8 runs at 65% avg util, FP8 78% —FP8 uses different kernels that keep more SMs busy but also can heat up memory bandwidth.
[12:10] [12:30] Ben Carter: If your constraint is cost, the console predicts monthly token cost and equivalent GPU hours. For Lumenary's trace INT8 predicted $11k/month, FP8 $14k/month — rough ballpark.
[12:52] Sara Kim: So 25% cost increase for better tail and lower error. Might be worth it.
[12:58] [13:10] Priya Nair: We also show sensitivity: if you add KV cache warming or prefix caching, INT8 p99 improves by ~80-120ms on our tests.
[13:32] Tina Park: Do you do any model-specific tuning? Our models are slightly modified from upstream.
[13:40] Priya Nair: We support model onboarding — light re-cal or per-model qprofiles. For custom forks we recommend a short calibration set (2-3k samples) and a sanity check in sandbox.
[14:00] [14:20] Ben Carter: Question for Lumenary: what is your acceptable P95/P99?
[14:25] Jamie Ortiz: target P95 under 200ms, P99 under 500ms; tolerance for morning spikes up to 1s for a short window.
[14:36] Ben Carter: ok that aligns with the runs we showed.
[14:40] [15:00] Priya Nair: Quick detour — autoscale behavior. If you use burst capacity, the system can offload high percentile traffic to a higher-tier pool (FP8 or dedicated) while keeping steady state on INT8.
[15:18] Miguel Alvarez: how do we instrument that? SLOs?
[15:23] Priya Nair: We use route-level SLOs; you set thresholds and actions. Instrumentation is via tracing hooks and token-level cost breakdown in the console.
[15:40] [16:00] Ben Carter: I'm going to demo a failure scenario — cold KV cache after deploy. Watch p99.
[16:10] Priya Nair: Simulating cold now. INT8 cold p99 jumped to 880ms in this sim, FP8 cold p99 720ms. Adding warm-up policy reduces cold p99 to 420ms / 360ms respectively.
[16:36] Sara Kim: Warm-up policy — is that pre-warming or synthetic traffic?
[16:42] Priya Nair: You can schedule warm-ups (synthetic requests) before traffic windows, or use passive prefetch when a prefix pattern is seen. We also support Tracing-based warm-up after deploy.
[16:58] [17:20] Jamie Ortiz: Concern: pre-warm sounds like extra cost.
[17:24] Ben Carter: yes but compare vs user impact of 1s tail. We often do targeted prefix warm-ups for top 10% heavy prefixes.
[17:35] [17:50] Priya Nair: Ok moving to the risk matrix: we map regression probability vs cost delta. For Lumenary's critical clinical paths we recommend FP8 for those routes and INT8 for lower-risk summarization.
[18:05] Tina Park: How do we operationalize per-route controls?
[18:10] Priya Nair: Routes are first-class in console. You can assign qprofiles per route, pin model versions, and set rollout policies (canary %, auto-rollback).
[18:28] [18:45] Ben Carter: We'll upload the sample heatmap and the CSV with per-route recommendations after the call.
[18:52] [19:10] Priya Nair: Quick Q about regulations — we have VPC options and can run this in Private deployment if audit logs and KMS are required.
[19:22] Jamie Ortiz: We will probably need Private for PHI handling. Are there config diffs for quantization in Private?
[19:30] Priya Nair: No functional difference; only control plane and network model changes. Runtime optimizations are the same across hosted and private.
[19:45] [20:00] Miguel Alvarez: Any known differences for on-prem GPUs? we use older Ampere nodes.
[20:06] Priya Nair: Kernel availability varies — some FP8 kernels require newer cu libraries. We provide a compatibility matrix and can recommend a quant profile for your hardware.
[20:22] Sara Kim: Can you share that matrix?
[20:25] Priya Nair: Yes will attach link: https://redwood.ai/compatibility-matrix (note: sample link).
[20:38] [21:00] Ben Carter: Ok let's walk through a hypothetical rollout: Week 0 calibrate qprofile with 2k samples; Week 1 run 10% traffic to INT8 with FP8 fallback; Week 2 increase to 50% if quality stable.
[21:22] Jamie Ortiz: Who runs the calibration — us or Redwood?
[21:27] Priya Nair: We can run it for you in the sandbox and hand over the qprofile. Calibration is a short job we can run as part of pilot.
[21:40] [22:00] Tina Park: About monitoring — what alerting options for quality regressions?
[22:06] Priya Nair: You can get alerts in Slack, PagerDuty, or email. We also export metrics to your Prometheus if you want.
[22:20] [22:40] Ben Carter: Time for some Q/A from Lumenary team.
[22:45] Sara Kim: On data retention: if we use hosted, do you keep prompts/outputs?
[22:51] Ben Carter: By default we retain logs for 30 days; enterprise plans can extend or disable retention for compliance. We also support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[23:06] Jamie Ortiz: SOC2 docs?
[23:09] Ben Carter: Yes we'll send SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
[23:15] [23:35] Miguel Alvarez: About benchmarking — can we run an A/B on our exact model fork?
[23:40] Priya Nair: Yes, we can onboard your fork in sandbox and run bench apples-to-apples. Might need a small VM for calibration.
[23:56] [24:20] Ben Carter: We're getting a few cross-talk items; I'm going to post links in the chat: sandbox invite, qprofile template, bench script.
[24:32] Priya Nair: Small demo of the optimizer's "auto-suggest": it looks at your trace and suggests profile X for chat routes and Y for summarization. It also gives an expected quality delta distribution.
[24:50] [25:10] Priya Nair: Note: suggestions are probabilistic; we always recommend a short pilot to validate.
[25:22] Tina Park: Anything about latency compensation if we do speculative parallel?
[25:28] Priya Nair: Yes speculative parallel reduces tail but increases cost ~30-60% depending on overlap. Our console shows the expected cost delta before you enable.
[25:45] [26:10] Ben Carter: I'm going to show an example alert when the quality monitor trips.
[26:18] [26:30] Priya Nair: Alert comes with diffs and example failing prompts. You can auto-route those to FP8 for reprocess and human review.
[26:45] [27:00] Sara Kim: How long to rollback?
[27:03] Priya Nair: Rollbacks are typically seconds — console has a one-click rollback that swaps route to previous model version or profile.
[27:12] [27:30] Jamie Ortiz: Ok we're almost at 30min mark — can we prioritize next steps?
[27:36] Ben Carter: Yes, recap: we'll send sandbox, run initial INT8/FP8 bench with Sara's sample trace, Priya will configure quality monitors and suggest per-route profiles.
[27:52] [28:10] Priya Nair: For the bench I'll need a 2-3k sample of prompts including edge cases. Also any domain-specific classifiers you want used for quality checks.
[28:27] Sara Kim: I'll upload dataset to the sandbox S3 link you provide.
[28:33] Miguel Alvarez: I'll share SLO doc and infra contact for Private details.
[28:40] [29:00] Ben Carter: Quick aside — competitors. Some customers ask about Anthropic and Cohere; our differentiator is the unified runtime+controls and transparent benching.
[29:14] Tina Park: Are there customers in healthcare doing exactly this?
[29:19] Ben Carter: yes we've pilot customers in medtech and a couple of EHR platforms — happy to share redacted case studies.
[29:28] [30:00] Priya Nair: Running a second set of bench sweeps now to show cost-sensitivity. Int8 with caching on improves p99 by ~100ms, but FP8 still holds better quality.
[30:22] [30:45] Priya Nair: I'm going to switch to the sandbox to show per-request traces. (small pause) Here is a request trace where fallback triggered — you can see the classifier fired and route changed to FP8, then human review queued.
[31:05] Sara Kim: Nice. Can we get a CSV of these traces?
[31:08] Priya Nair: Yes will export as CSV from the trace UI.
[31:20] [31:45] Ben Carter: A question from Tina: what's the recommended way to handle mixed-criticality routes?
[31:50] Priya Nair: Best practice: categorize routes by criticality, assign FP8 to critical and INT8 for non-critical. Use canaries and quality monitors for transitions. Also consider speculative parallel only on high-criticality routes.
[32:12] Miguel Alvarez: On cost reporting — will we see token-level cost per route?
[32:18] Ben Carter: Yes, console has per-route token and $ breakdown.
[32:28] [32:50] Sara Kim: Are there any gotchas for long context windows? we use up to 8k tokens.
[32:56] Priya Nair: Long context interacts with KV cache and memory; quantization impact can be non-linear on very long sequences. We recommend FP8 for >4k in many cases, but it's model dependent.
[33:20] [33:40] Ben Carter: Priya, can you run a quick sensitivity sweep across temperature and max tokens?
[33:45] Priya Nair: Running sweep: higher temp marginally increases hallucination risk on INT8; FP8 degrades less with temp increase. Max tokens increase increases p99 proportionally due to more tokens.
[34:08] [34:30] Jamie Ortiz: Ok that's useful.
[34:34] Tina Park: Any impact on embeddings if we quantize?
[34:40] Priya Nair: We separate embeddings service; quantization affects generation models primarily. We don't recommend INT8 for embeddings where vector quality is critical.
[34:58] [35:20] Ben Carter: We have about 20 minutes left, want to demo the pilot template.
[35:26] Priya Nair: Pilot template includes calibration job, bench script, quality monitor config, rollback plan, and a cost estimate.
[35:40] [36:00] Priya Nair: I'm going to open the template now and walk through each artifact. (screen gestures)
[36:20] [36:45] Priya Nair: Calibration job: takes your sample, runs per-layer stats, produces qprofile and a summary HTML with flagged outliers.
[36:58] Sara Kim: How long does calibration take?
[37:02] Priya Nair: Usually 20-40 minutes for a 2k sample set, depends on model size.
[37:16] [37:30] Ben Carter: For next steps, we propose: sandbox access now, calibration this week, bench results early next week, then pilot kickoff.
[37:44] Miguel Alvarez: works for infra. I'll block time.
[37:50] [38:10] Ben Carter: Any final technical questions?
[38:14] Sara Kim: One last — if we see a persistent regression on INT8, can we automatically pin only certain layers to FP16 while keeping rest INT8?
[38:25] Priya Nair: Yes, partial quantization / layer pinning is supported. That's a middle ground often used when a handful of sensitive layers cause regression.
[38:40] [39:00] Ben Carter: Alright wrapping up — I'll recap actions.
[39:06] Ben Carter: 1) Send sandbox invite and qprofile CSV (Ben) 2) Run bench INT8/FP8 on your trace (Priya) 3) Lumenary to upload trace + SLO doc (Sara/Miguel) 4) PRDs and compliance artifacts (Ben)
[39:30] Jamie Ortiz: Sounds good.
[39:34] [40:00] Priya Nair: I'll also attach the bench logs and CSVs to the sandbox. Expect initial bench artifact by Friday.
[40:12] Ben Carter: Any blockers?
[40:17] Miguel Alvarez: none from infra side once we get the invite.
[40:22] Tina Park: product side good.
[40:28] [41:00] Ben Carter: Ok thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links and schedule the pilot kickoff next week.
[41:16] Jamie Ortiz: Thanks Ben, Priya.
[41:20] Sara Kim: Thanks all.
[41:22] Miguel Alvarez: bye.
[41:25] Tina Park: bye.
[41:30] Meeting end

References shared in chat: sandbox invite (https://redwood.app/sandbox/rdw-47821), qprofile template CSV (https://redwood.app/sandbox/qprofile-template.csv), compatibility matrix (https://redwood.ai/compatibility-matrix).
